name: Open Builder Score
description: Open, deterministic builder reputation score computable client-side from public data. Multipliers started from Talent Protocol's finalized 2025 season; deviations from those weights are deliberate and recorded in the changelog. The credential set is deliberately narrower than production, counting only evidence of shipping and peer recognition. Credentials that score attendance, membership, token balances or testnet activity are kept in this file with status "excluded" and a reason, so what is left out stays as legible as what is counted.

changelog.0.3.0: Re-cut eth_global_finalist from binary 10 to the judged-results curve (15 x sqrt(distinct finalist events), cap 30) so the only judged EthGlobal credential no longer prices below the participation packs; capped the frozen Base Devfolio manifests at their attainable maxima (participation 20 to 17, won 30 to 26 - only 3 contracts exist); halved github_repositories (multiplier 2 to 1, cap 8 to 4) as the cheapest-to-farm credential; moved github_forks, github_repositories and talent_protocol_verified_builder from sum_all to max_value to close multi-account stacking. Max total: 276 to 285.
changelog.0.2.0: Reused ambiguously for two different credential sets: 15 active / 196 points, then 18 active / 276 points when the three NFT-metadata credentials were activated without a version bump. Attestations recorded before that activation were computed under the 196-point set; verification keys on the version string alone and cannot tell the two apart.

calculation_modes.sum_all: sum raw values across all connected accounts FIRST, then convert, then multiply
calculation_modes.max_value: convert and multiply per account, take the best account

scoring.determinism: all values are read at an as-of anchor (timestamp + block number per chain); the anchor is included in any attestation

tiers.rpc: pure RPC reads (balanceOf, contract calls) — zero infrastructure
tiers.indexed: requires a public indexer or token-metadata enumeration (EAS GraphQL, NFT metadata walk)
tiers.github_public: GitHub REST, unauthenticated (60 req/hr per IP)

credentials.name: ETHGlobal Finalist
credentials.notes: 0.3.0 re-cut: the only judged EthGlobal credential was priced below the participation packs (binary 10 vs Hacker 12, Builder 20). Now mirrors devfolio_hackathons_won's curve; counted as distinct finalist contracts so repeat tokens from one event cannot inflate

credentials.name: Devfolio Hackathons Won
credentials.notes: same contracts as participation, filtered by token metadata attribute nft_type == WINNER — needs tokenURI enumeration. A win intentionally also earns participation (win ⊃ participate): one won event pays 15 here + 10 there

credentials.name: Base Hackathons Participation
credentials.notes: 0.3.0: cap lowered 20 → 17 = round(10×sqrt(3)) — only 3 contracts exist and the manifest is frozen, so 20 was unreachable. Raising the cap again requires new events and a rebuilt allowlist, which is a version bump anyway

credentials.name: Base Hackathons Won
credentials.notes: WINNER metadata filter, as devfolio_hackathons_won. 0.3.0: cap lowered 30 → 26 = round(15×sqrt(3)) — only 3 contracts exist in the frozen manifest, so 30 was unreachable

credentials.name: Encode Programmes Participation
credentials.status_reason: Same source problem as encode_programmes_won: the explorer truncates the collection and its holder count disagrees with a sweep of its own data, so a build cannot be checked against anything.
credentials.notes: single contract; programme_type + accreditation_level read from token metadata — needs enumeration

credentials.name: Encode Programmes Won
credentials.status_reason: Readable in principle, deliberately not scored: the only source that serves the metadata in bulk is an explorer that returns 8,910 of the 14,432 tokens and reports a holder count its own data contradicts, so no build of it can be validated.

credentials.name: Basecamp Attendee
credentials.notes: SBTs are ERC-1155 and production reads them from its NFT indexer (WalletNFT/TrackedNFT), not RPC balanceOf — mis-tiered as rpc in the original extraction; needs token-id enumeration post-POC. Survives the attendance exclusion that removed FarCon because Basecamp admission is application-gated builder selection, not an open ticket purchase

credentials.name: Base Learn
credentials.status_reason: The completion SBTs live on Base Sepolia, and testnet credentials are cheap to farm.

credentials.name: Speed Run Ethereum Challenges
credentials.notes: NOT onchain — BuidlGuidl public API by wallet address; verify CORS, else defer

credentials.name: Farcon NYC 2025 Attendee
credentials.status_reason: Conference attendance is a ticket purchase, not building.

credentials.name: D_D Member
credentials.status_reason: Scores a $CODE balance, which is buyable on the open market.

credentials.name: $TALENT Balance
credentials.status_reason: Scores a $TALENT balance, which is buyable — and it is our own token.

credentials.name: $TALENT Vault
credentials.status_reason: Scores a $TALENT deposit, which is buyable — and it is our own token.

credentials.name: Verified Onchain Builder
credentials.notes: EAS attestations by recipient — enumeration needs the public EAS GraphQL indexer (easscan), not a raw RPC. 0.3.0: sum_all → max_value; one attester already saturated the cap, so the sum was decorative and would only have re-counted the same attester across wallets

credentials.name: GitHub Forks
credentials.notes: 0.3.0: sum_all → max_value — identical for a single handle, but summing across handles would let sock accounts stack the most farmable GitHub metric

credentials.name: GitHub Repositories
credentials.notes: approximation — production counts repos contributed-to (needs auth); disclose in UI. 0.3.0: halved (multiplier 2 → 1, cap 8 → 4) and sum_all → max_value — empty public repos are the cheapest farm in the set, ~10 minutes for the old 8 points
